title: Cost, Visas Shape Students' Study-Abroad Choices
paragraphs: For many young people, studying in another country is an exciting opportunity. However, according to new research, decisions about where to study, or whether to study abroad at all, are increasingly being shaped by visa rules and costs.

The research, called Emerging Futures 9, was carried out by IDP Education, a company that helps international students apply to universities, and published in May 2026. It surveyed more than 5,800 current and prospective international students in 118 countries and regions.

One of the clearest findings was that students are now comparing more options before making a decision. According to the survey, 78% of students compare several countries before choosing where to study, up from 66% in October 2024. Meanwhile, among students who had completely given up on their plans to study abroad, 26% said that it was because getting a visa was too difficult, compared with 20% in the previous survey. In addition, 27% of these students said that the cost of visas was a major barrier.

Simon Emmett, an executive at IDP, explained that visa issues used to come up late in the process of planning to study abroad, but "now we're hearing from students that it's one of the first things they check." If students cannot get a visa for one country, he said, "many will simply move on to a country where they can." In his view, students today are "screening countries the way a consumer screens a product."

According to the research, interest in some traditional destinations is changing. Australia appears to be strengthening, while Canada is stabilizing after a period of uncertainty. On the other hand, early interest in the UK, the US and New Zealand has declined somewhat. At the same time, countries such as Germany, France and China are becoming increasingly competitive. Nevertheless, Emmett emphasized that the traditional destinations "aren't going anywhere."
The research suggests that clear information about visa processing times and financial requirements is becoming an important advantage for countries that want to attract international students.
